criteria.description: The existing OAuth flow authorizes through deterministic doubles and permits repository selection without live GitHub access.
verification: Start the product with the operator database and a deterministic OAuth/GitHub double that returns repositories A and B plus a unique fake token canary.
From `/settings/github`, complete Continue with GitHub and return through the existing callback.
Verify the settings page displays repositories A and B and allows A to be selected.
Verify the GitHub double journal shows the expected authorization/token and repository-list interactions, with no request to live GitHub.

criteria.description: The OAuth access token is not exposed to the browser or logs after OAuth completes.
verification: Use the fake token canary while capturing browser request/response traffic, console output, and backend/frontend process logs from callback completion through loading and saving repository settings.
Verify the canary is absent from the final address-bar URL and every browser-observed request URL.
Verify the canary is absent from rendered page text/HTML and every readable browser-observed HTTP response body.
Verify every key and value in both `localStorage` and `sessionStorage` lacks the canary.
Verify the canary is absent from browser console output and captured backend/frontend logs.

criteria.description: The selected repository survives a real backend restart using the same operator SQLite database.
verification: Complete OAuth against the operator database, select repository A, and confirm A is shown as selected.
Terminate the backend process without replacing or resetting the database.
Start a new backend process against that exact operator database path and reload `/settings/github`.
Verify A is still shown as selected without selecting it again or repeating OAuth.

criteria.description: Changing selection from A to B makes the next manual scan target B while previously created A work remains associated with A.
verification: With A selected in the operator database, start a manual scan and retain its resulting A-targeted work record.
Change the selected repository to B, clear the GitHub double request journal, and click the existing Scan now control.
Verify the next scan completes against B and the double journal contains B-targeted requests with no A-targeted request for that new scan.
Reload or query the existing A work and verify its displayed/API-visible repository is still A.

criteria.description: After selection changes to B, the next due scheduled scan targets B exactly as the manual scan does.
verification: Keep B selected, enable a deterministically due schedule, and clear the GitHub double request journal.
Drive the real scheduler path with the controlled acceptance-test clock or due-schedule harness.
Verify one scheduled scan is created for B and reaches the expected observable result.
Verify the double journal contains B-targeted requests and no A-targeted request for that scheduled scan.

criteria.description: Changing the current selection to B never retargets reconcile, rollback, approval, or publish actions for existing A work.
verification: Prepare A-targeted records in the operator database in states where reconcile, rollback, approval, and publication are each applicable, then select B.
Perform each action through its existing UI or API entry point and inspect the resulting workflow state and GitHub double journal.
Verify every GitHub interaction caused by each existing-work action names repository A, never B.
Verify the records remain API/UI-visible as A-targeted after the actions complete.

criteria.description: All existing backend, frontend unit, browser acceptance, and production-build checks remain green.
verification: Run `.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q` and expect exit code 0.
Run `npm --prefix frontend test` and expect exit code 0.
Run `npm --prefix frontend run test:e2e` with provisioned browser binaries and expect exit code 0.
Run `npm --prefix frontend run build` and expect exit code 0.

note: The definition of done. Later phases may ONLY flip `passes`. Editing or removing a criterion is a gate failure.
